claims.exact_statement: For an even periodic cubic torus of side L>=4, V=L^3, spin S in {1/2,1,3/2,...}, and spin-isotropic nearest-neighbor couplings J_i>0, the shifted ferromagnetic Hamiltonian K=sum_{x,i} J_i(S^2 I-S_x dot S_{x+e_i}) satisfies K|_{Jtot=SV-d} >= (S min_i J_i/(6L^2)) d for every total-spin sector d=SV-Jtot.
assumptions: Three-dimensional cubic periodic graph, all three directions present
Fixed positive J_i and a common spin S at every site
Each bond is SU(2)-invariant scalar exchange; no field or spin-space anisotropy
claims.status: internal derivation from a published source lemma; not independently externally reviewed
claims.novelty_boundary: CGS Prop. 5.2 already proves an open-box O(S L^-2) total-spin sector gap by the same local three-spin/path mechanism. This report derives an explicit periodic routing constant and a min-coupling anisotropic comparison; no novelty or priority claim is made.

costs.input: S, L, and calibrated lower exchange bound Jmin=min_i J_i are supplied
costs.proof_arithmetic: O(V^2 L) routed-pair terms conceptually; finite geometry was exhaustively checked only for L=4,6,8
costs.physical_measurement: Not needed to state the mathematical gap; exchange calibration is required to apply it to a specimen

claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the three-spin inequality or a directed-edge routing count exceeding L^4 invalidates the constant; the analytic count is in PROOF.md and finite checks are in checks/.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review; then obtain a fixed-beta finite-volume bound on normalized total-spin deficit rather than use the whole-torus L^-2 gap.

claims.exact_statement: For any 0<r<=1, beta >= (6L^2/(S Jmin)) log(2V/log(1+r)) implies Zexc/Zground<=r, P(Jtot<SV)<=r/(1+r), and W1(Law(M^3/V),Unif[-S,S])<=1/(3V)+S r/(2(1+r)); the state is the exact zero-field SU(2)-invariant Gibbs state on the weighted periodic torus.
assumptions: Inverse temperature beta satisfies the stated size-dependent sufficient bound
Equilibrium Gibbs sampling for statistical use; equilibration time is not proved
claims.status: internal corollary of c7_weighted_periodic_sector_gap and exact SU(2) representation counting
claims.proof_path: PROOF.md, sector count, Gibbs tail, and observable conversion sections
claims.novelty_boundary: This proves a joint low-temperature/finite-volume ground-multiplet regime. It does not prove a fixed-beta rate to m_{beta,J}; the leading path lemma and binomial sector counting are prior art. Priority unknown.

claims.exact_statement: Assuming the pinned anisotropic Bloch-law source applies and 0<=m_{beta,J}<=S, the same Gibbs law satisfies W1(Law(M^3/V),Unif[-m_{beta,J},m_{beta,J}]) <= 1/(3V)+S r/(2(1+r))+(S-m_{beta,J})/2 under the extreme-cooling condition. The source asymptotic implies this tends to zero along V->infinity, r->0, beta->infinity, but gives no effective finite-beta remainder for the last term.
assumptions: The pinned family-271 anisotropic Bloch-law statement is valid for the chosen J_i and m_{beta,J} tends to S
claims.status: internal triangle inequality conditional on a source-reported low-temperature limit; asymptotic only
claims.novelty_boundary: The source provides an ordered-limit Bloch asymptotic, not a finite-beta numerical remainder or fixed-beta finite-volume spherical law. This is not an effective specimen budget.

claims.exact_statement: On the weighted periodic torus, the M^3=SV-1 one-magnon band has energies epsilon(k)=2S sum_i J_i(1-cos(2pi k_i/L)); its nonzero modes imply Zexc/Zground >= ((2SV-1)/(2SV+1)) sum_{k!=0} exp(-beta epsilon(k)). At each fixed beta>0 the right-hand side is Theta(V), so the ground-multiplet Gibbs probability tends to zero.
assumptions: S>0, J_i>0, beta fixed positive as L increases
claims.status: exact one-magnon representation calculation; internal derivation
claims.novelty_boundary: This concerns ground-sector mass only. It does not refute convergence of the normalized total-spin radius or the finite-temperature spherical law; excited spin-wave density can be extensive but submacroscopic.

claims.exact_statement: A half-up/half-down spin-coherent product state on the periodic cube has shifted energy expectation 4 S^2 J_1 L^2, energy density tending zero, and <M^2>=SV. Its SU(2)-averaged density matrix preserves these quantities and is rotation invariant, yet E[Jtot/V]<=sqrt(S/V)->0.
assumptions: Even periodic L, with two flat domain interfaces normal to direction 1
Spin-coherent product state on the two half-cubes, followed optionally by global SU(2) averaging
claims.status: exact counterexample to an energy-density-only inference; it is not a Gibbs-state counterexample

claims.novelty_boundary: Does not refute the periodic Gibbs theorem. It shows why local block order, vanishing energy density, and SU(2) invariance alone cannot replace a Gibbs-specific orientation-alignment argument.
